feat(binds): toggle monocle with <meta-h> (<meta-m> on colemak_dh)

Makes it behave like Hyprland on my desktop, and Aerospace on my work
Mac, where partial full screen/monocle mode is something you can toggle
on or off with the same key. Previously in my DWM setup I had a
different key for monocle mode and tiling mode, which is annoying now
that my different environments have started to drift and my muscle
memory becomes unreliable.

feat: switch to kitty terminal

It's what I use on my nixos desktop, and nix-darwin work laptop. It's
got nice font rendering, and tabs can be useful sometimes after all.

I really want to migrate to NixOS on my laptop, but I kind of want to
figure out secret management, full disk encryption and declarative disk
partitioning first.
git: merge upstream branch 'master' into custom

!feat: launch script renames and improvements

Includes new hacks to keep the terminal around after the original CLI
program is closed. Useful when I launch the `nnn` terminal file manager
and press crtl+g to cd-on-quit into the opened directory. Previously, if
`nnn` was launched through a DWM shortcut, the terminal would then just
close because the command was finished. Now it spawns a regular bash
session instead. So now I can use cd-on-quit like I'm used to when
launching `nnn` through a hotkey.

Also adapts to renamed scripts. I changed `launch_cmus.sh` (and others)
to `st_cmus.sh`, to make it more clear that they spawn a terminal.

In a way, this pattern launches interactive CLI programs from a
non-interactive context. Like when called by a window manager or dmenu.

feat: disable floating layout, clean up commented code

I sometimes float individual windows, but never all of them. So I have
no use for a floating layout. Removing the hotkeys frees them for future
use, and prevents occasionally triggering them on accident in the
meantime.

Also removes some binds I had previously commented out.

which makes it conflict with my customized version, so I had to rename

is fine but not consistent with the original code. Besides, vim's native

feat(patch): applied xtile

Xtile is like flextile, in the sense that it's not a particular layout,
but a way of customizing the layout strategies by changing the relation
between the main and stack areas and the relation between clients
either in the main or stack areas.

Unlike flextile it also comes with a kind of cfacts of its own. But it
only affects the first (or last?) client in each area, as opposed to just
any client you want.

Unlike flextile it doesn't have a deck style layout. The author seems to
have a rather strong opinion, and believes micromanaging the order of
clients in the stack is an anti-pattern. The deck layout has an annoying
quirk of leaving a different client on top, depending on whether you
leave the deck using the j or k key. The author's suggestion is to
rather use tags if you want to hide a client, which is excellent advice.

Not only can you select what tags to assign a client to, you can also
select whatever combination of tags you want in view. So you can assign
just one, or maybe a few, clients to each tag, and then select and
deselect whatever combination of tags, depending on what clients you
want in view.

fix(lsp): move `lsp` rtdir to `after/` & disable harper-ls for code

As per https://github.com/neovim/neovim/discussions/35819#discussioncomment-14432142

Turns out, in order to overwrite the configs provided by lspconfig, one
has to place their `lsp/*.lua` files under the `after/` directory.
Now my harper-ls is properly configured to only work on prose related
file types, as opposed to running on the comments of most coding
file types where it would produce way to many false positives.

Also configures the dialect used by harper, so now ltex-plus and harper
finally agree.
